correctness.rationale: I enumerated automorphisms of the seven-point Fano incidence structure independently as permutations preserving triples {a,b,a xor b}, and composed permutations rather than using the frozen matrix product. These are exactly GL_3(F_2): preserving the third point of the line through distinct nonzero vectors preserves addition, also for equal vectors and zero. Starting at the identity subgroup I generated extensions by adjoining whole cosets of the current subgroup under right multiplication by one extra generator. This reaches exactly each generated subgroup, and induction on generators gives completeness. I recovered 168 group elements, 179 subgroups including endpoints, and unquotiented flag counts (177,911,1071,336). Simultaneous conjugation gives (13,37,37,12) orbits. Strictly increasing subgroup orders imply that two points of a single closed simplex can be orbit-equivalent only if they coincide: their positive-support faces must have the same order set, hence the same vertices inside that simplex, and conjugation preserves the corresponding barycentric coordinates. This proves regular simplex closures in the quotient and justifies the reconstructed facet maps; individual subgroup-conjugacy classes are not used as a substitute for flag orbits. Independent enumeration found every nonempty proper face of each orbit cell, and all 49 archived pairs removed an active codimension-one face with exactly one active strict coface, leaving vertex 6. A separate greedy sequence also removed 49 pairs and left vertex 11. Each removal is an elementary collapse since the upper cell is an embedded simplex and the removed face has no other coface. value.rationale: This finite classification concerns the full proper subgroup lattice of the second-smallest nonabelian simple group, a natural test beyond A5. The original subgroup complex has nontrivial first homology, and the ordinary quotient actually collapses, a stronger fact than trivial homology or Euler characteristic one. The exact flag incidence and cancellation data give a reproducible comparison with documented noncontractible neighboring examples, without claiming a broader classification.
